claim_verdicts.evidence: Carried from prior review (claim unchanged). "The reclaim policy for a PersistentVolume tells the cluster what to do with the volume after it has been released of its claim. Currently, volumes can either be Retained, Recycled, or Deleted." Field name persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy confirmed in the PersistentVolume API reference and in reclaim-policy.sh line 10. (Local mirror is the v1.37 site; section unchanged in substance for 1.34.)

Carried from prior review (claim unchanged). "If no reclaimPolicy is specified ... it will default to Delete." Binding mode (added in round 2): "specifying the WaitForFirstConsumer mode which will delay the binding and provisioning of a PersistentVolume until a Pod using the PersistentVolumeClaim is created." kind's standard: captured output "standard (default)   rancher.io/local-path   Delete".

Carried from prior review (claim unchanged). Round 2: lesson now says the volume "disappears from kubectl get pv, and the storage behind it is deleted with it"; the unsourced local-path folder detail is gone. Docs: "deletion removes both the PersistentVolume object from Kubernetes, as well as the associated storage asset in the external infrastructure."

Carried from prior review (claim unchanged). "When the PersistentVolumeClaim is deleted, the PersistentVolume still exists and the volume is considered \"released\". But it is not yet available for another claim because the previous claimant's data remains on the volume. An administrator can manually reclaim the volume"

Round 2026-11-09, version_key local_path_provisioner. README is silent on Retain: it only shows `reclaimPolicy: Delete` in StorageClass examples (WebFetch). Verdict rests on execution: captured stage-3 run, after `kubectl delete pvc data kept`: "kept    retain-local   Retain    Released", no data line. K8s phase: "Released: the claim has been deleted, but the associated storage resource is not yet reclaimed".

Carried from prior review (claim unchanged). Docs recovery procedure: "Delete the claimRef entry from PV specs, so as new PVC can bind to it. This should make the PV Available." — so a Released PV keeps claimRef and is not bound until it is removed. Retain: "not yet available for another claim". Output: CLAIM column (.spec.claimRef.name) still reads kept after the claim is deleted.

Carried from prior review (claim unchanged). "This deletes _everything_ under the namespace!" and "low-level resources, such as Nodes and PersistentVolumes, are not in any namespace." Output: after `kubectl delete namespace storage-lessons` the list has no data line.

Carried from prior review (claim unchanged). "automated sync will not delete resources when Argo CD detects the resource is no longer defined in Git"; pruning "can also be enabled to happen automatically as part of the automated sync" with prune: true (WebFetch summary of stable docs, not a 3.1-pinned page). apps/staging.yaml at stage-3 lines 23-25: automated, selfHeal: true, prune: true.

Carried from prior review (claim unchanged). git show stage-3:deploy/k8s/lessons/retain-storageclass.yaml lines 8-11: name retain-local, provisioner rancher.io/local-path, reclaimPolicy Retain, volumeBindingMode WaitForFirstConsumer. Output shows standard with the same PROVISIONER and VOLUMEBINDINGMODE and marked (default); retain-local is not. Lesson now names both the name and default-class differences.

Carried from prior review (claim unchanged). Line numbers and copy correct (line 28 adds storageClassName: retain-local; 41-45, 50-56 as stated). Round 2: lesson now says "The Pod writer names both claims as its volumes", which matches sed line 30 adding a Pod-level volume for kept; the container-mount wording is gone.

Carried from prior review (claim unchanged). reclaim-policy.sh lines 9-12: custom-columns=CLAIM:.spec.claimRef.name,CLASS:.spec.storageClassName,RECLAIM:.spec.persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy,STATUS:.status.phase, then awk keeps the header and lines starting with data or kept.

Carried from prior review (claim unchanged). Output block in the lesson matches outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/reclaim-policy.txt line for line: data/kept Bound before; only "kept    retain-local   Retain    Released" after both deletions.

Round 2026-11-09, version_key local_path_provisioner. README does not cover deleting a Retain PV: "The volume content stored on the node will be automatically cleaned up" (after deleting pod+pvc of the Delete example) and "The teardown script is run after the volume is deleted, to cleanup the volume directory on the node", neither tied to reclaimPolicy. Only the script comment (reclaim-policy.sh:59) states the folder stays; cluster not inspected.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Round 2026-11-09, version_key local_path_provisioner. README: "the directory /opt/local-path-provisioner will be used across all the nodes as the path for provisioning (a.k.a, store the persistent volume data)"; "nodePathMap is the place user can customize where to store the data on each node"; "the volume is only accessible on the node where it was provisioned". kind docs (prior round): "The node is a container created by kind." Claim limited to kind.

Carried from prior review (claim unchanged). PersistentVolumeClaimSpec: "storageClassName is the name of the StorageClass required by the claim." The spec has no reclaim-policy field (none listed in the PersistentVolumeClaimSpec table); persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy exists only in PersistentVolumeSpec.

Carried from prior review (claim unchanged). persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy whenDeleted: "Retain (default)"; "The default for policies is Retain, matching the StatefulSet behavior before this new feature."

Carried from prior review (claim unchanged). Conditioned recommendation ("suits data you would rather clean up by hand than lose") with its cost stated; consistent with docs: Retain "allows for manual reclamation of the resource".

Carried from prior review (claim unchanged). Definitional distinction (backup = separate copy elsewhere). The factual support it leans on (copy lost with node/cluster) is kind-specific and is handled under claim 14.

issues.text: Claim 13 (local-path leaves the Released volume's folder after the PV is deleted) is still unverified: its new governing doc, the local-path-provisioner README, does not say what happens to the folder of a Retain PV that is deleted by hand. The lesson credits the script comment, so only minor.
issues.quote: its comment notes that the provisioner `rancher.io/local-path` leaves the `Released` volume's folder on its node even then
issues.fix: Either drop the clause from section 5 (and claim 13), or have the owner run reclaim-policy.sh and then `docker exec <node from the PV nodeAffinity> ls /var/local-path-provisioner` (path from the local-path-config ConfigMap) after the PV is deleted and record the listing in claim 13 source_hint.
